content.text:
All three renders are done and verified.

**Files in the working folder:**
- `portrait.png` — 1080×1350 (master, scale 1.0)
- `wide.png` — 1200×1000 (scale 0.85)
- `sky.png` — 300×600 (scale 0.28)
- `flyer.html` — single source template

**How it works:** one layout authored in master-logical pixels, wrapped in a `#root` sized `W/s × H/s` and `transform: scale(s)` — so every size is literally the master's design at the requested scale, just with a different logical canvas. Font loaded via `@font-face` from `Inter.ttf` (verified with `document.fonts.check`).

**Checks performed on each size:**
- Photo and CTA bars measure exactly full canvas width (300/1200/1080 px) at every size; side padding applies only to text sections.
- Photo uses `object-fit: cover`, so it crops (barn stays in frame) instead of distorting — it renders a tall band in portrait, a letterbox in wide, a short band in sky.
- Candidate columns are equal `flex: 1 1 0` cells, so they stay evenly spaced at all widths.
- `scrollHeight - clientHeight = 0` and `scrollWidth == clientWidth` on every element — no overflow, no clipping, no overlap.

**Defect found and fixed:** the sky version initially had maxed-out spacers, leaving ~75px of dead white at the top and bottom with the content floating in the middle. I made the spacer and photo max-heights proportional to the logical canvas height (`calc(var(--lh) * 0.07 / 0.09 / 0.32)`), so tall formats absorb leftover space into the rhythm. Sky now fills edge-to-edge with even 42px margins top and bottom; portrait and wide were re-rendered and are unchanged by the fix.
